simple.meaning: יָלַל (yâlal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to howl (with a wailing tone) or yell (with a boisterous one).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 31 times in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, Joel, and 4 more, beginning at Isaiah 13:6. The surrounding contexts include city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָלַל (H3213) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָלַל (yâlal) / H3213 is traced through Isaiah 13:6, Isaiah 14:31, Isaiah 15:2, Isaiah 15:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to howl (with a wailing tone) or yell (with a boisterous one)
definitions.full: H3213. yalal [ יָלַל ] verb Hiph`il howl, make a howling (onomatopoetic) — Hiph`il Perfect וְהֵילִל consecutive Jer 47:2 ; וְהֵילִיל֫וּ consecutive Amos 8:3 ; Imperfect יְיֵלִיל Isa 15:2-3 t. (Ges § 70 . 2, R. 2 Kö i. 437, 421 ); אֲיֵלִיל Jer 48:31 ; וְאֵילִי֫לָה Micah 1:8 ; יְיֵלִיל֫וּ Hosea 7:14 (Kö i. 421 ); יְהֵילִי֫לוּ Isa 52:5 ; תִּיִלִי֫לוּ 65:14 ; Imperative הֵילֵל Ezek 21:17 ; Zech 11:2 ; הֵילִי֫לִי Isa 14:31 ; 49:3 + Jer 48:20 Kt; הֵילִי֫לוּ Isa 13:6 13 t. + Jer 48:20 Qr, + Ezek 30:2 (strike out ᵐ5 Co); — utter or make a howling, give a howl , in distress, || זעק Hosea 7:14 ; Jer 47:2 ; Isa 14:31 ; Jer 25:34 ; 48:20 , 31 (followed by על ), Ezek 21:17 ; || צעק Isa 65:14 (followed by מִן of occasion, source); || ספד Micah 1:8 ; Jer 4:8 ; Joel 1:13 ; || הֹבִישׁ 1:11 ; || בכה 1:5 (compare Isa 15:2-3 ,+ בֶּ֑כִי ); followed by על Jer 51:8 ; Isa 15:2-3 , We proposes ילילו for יגילו Hosea 10:5 (others יחילו , see גיל above); followed by לְ Isa 16:7 ; absolute היכל שׁירות והילילו Amos 8:3 and palace-songs shall become howlings , Isa 13:6 ; 16:7 ; 23:1 , 6 , 14 ; Jer 48:39 ; 49:3 ( Ezek 30:2 see above), Zeph 1:11 ; Zech 11:2 (twice in verse); in cruel exultation Isa 52:5 compare De Che di. — On בֶּןשָֿׁ֑חַר הֵילֵל 14:12 compare below I. הלל above.

occurrences.englishText: Wail, for Yahweh’s day is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.
Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.
They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.
In their streets, they clothe themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.
Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.
Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.
The burden of Tyre.
Pass over to Tarshish! Wail, you inhabitants of the coast!
Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!
“Now therefore, what do I do here,” says Yahweh,
Behold, my servants will sing for joy of heart,
For this, clothe yourself with sackcloth, lament and wail; for the fierce anger of Yahweh hasn’t turned back from us.
Wail, you shepherds, and cry.
Yahweh says:
Moab is disappointed;
Moab is disappointed;
Therefore I will wail for Moab.
“How it is broken down!
“Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste!
Babylon has suddenly fallen and been destroyed!
I will also strike my hands together,
“Son of man, prophesy, and say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says:
They haven’t cried to me with their heart,
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep!
Be confounded, you farmers!
Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests!
The songs of the temple will be wailing in that day,” says the Lord Yahweh.
For this I will lament and wail;
Wail, you inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the people of Canaan are undone! All those who were loaded with silver are cut off.
Wail, cypress tree, for the cedar has fallen,
